title: Transport forced cover vertices to minimum-true CNF models
claim: Let a satisfy the positive edge CNF of a finite simple graph G, and suppose a minimizes the number of true variables among graph vertices. If a vertex v has degree greater than that minimum count, the selected theorem proves a(v)=true and that the same assignment satisfies the edge CNF with v-incident clauses removed. The proof transports the known vertex-cover forcing result into the list-CNF representation and directly uses the declared exact B artifact for the deletion equality.
novelty: The forced-vertex fact is already established by upstream L_meta_727. Local work identifies trueVars of a satisfying assignment with a vertex cover, constructs an assignmentOf for every finite cover, proves the relevant cardinality correspondence, and transfers the minimum-cardinality hypothesis. It applies the upstream forcing theorem, then invokes B.graphCNF_delete_vertex on the original assignment. This is a formal integration of a known consequence using an explicit local dependency, not a new literature result or stronger complexity theorem.

prior_art.relationship: Exact source of the vertex-cover forcing theorem and its proof; the submitted CNF statement is a known consequence expressed through the local representation.
The upstream graph restriction theorem enters through B, whose exact selected deletion theorem is called in the C proof.
